body:
## Ask

Future-proof the PostgreSQL ledger against storage constraints with **fully aggressive, fully optimized sharding**, and give operators a three-tier retention scheme plus an opt-in archival role — so a ledger that grows forever never forces a choice between truth and disk.

## The three modes (all configurable, all lossless by definition)

1. **Standard mode (the official default)** — the latest **N full, uncompressed ledger records**, N > 0 and operator-configured. Hot reads stay raw: no decompression on the working set, ever.
2. **Mid-tier mode** — the latest **N ledger records under aggressive *and* lossless compression**, N operator-configured. Aggressive and lossless are both load-bearing: maximum ratio, zero information loss, bit-for-bit reconstructible.
3. **Archival mode** — the **full ledger since inception** as one aggressively-and-losslessly compressed dataset. Nothing is ever unrecoverable; the entire history reconstructs bit-for-bit.

Records age through the tiers automatically: raw in standard, compressed at mid-tier, folded into the archive — with the tier boundaries (both Ns) as ordinary config.

## The opt-in archival node

A deployment may opt in to running a **full archival node**: it holds the complete since-inception ledger (mode 3) alongside the hot tiers, serving history that other nodes have compacted away. Opt-in per the no-guarantees family of doctrines — and note the 10.a resonance: full archival nodes are how ledgers survive attempts to erase them. A non-archival node keeps only its configured standard + mid-tier windows plus the archive segments it has produced.

## Sharding requirements

- **Declarative partitioning** on the ledger's natural key (sequence/time), hash- or range-based as benchmarks dictate — chosen for pruning efficiency, not fashion.
- Partition rotation automated (creation, tier transition, archive fold-in) with zero operator ceremony after configuration.
- **Chunking + content-addressed hashing** for the compressed tiers: identical chunks dedupe, every chunk's hash chains into the ledger's own integrity story, and archive verification is a hash walk, not a full decompress.
- Compression candidates to benchmark: zstd (high levels) on columnar-organized segments, PostgreSQL-native options (TOAST tuning, lz4/zstd column compression) for mid-tier, external content-addressed segment files for the archive. Pick by measured ratio × restore-speed, document the numbers.

## Acceptance

- All three modes configurable and covered by tests that prove **bit-for-bit reconstruction** from mid-tier and archival forms.
- Tier transitions exercised under load; a query spanning all three tiers returns one coherent, correct answer.
- Archival-node opt-in documented never-lost style: what it stores, what it serves, what it costs.
- Benchmarks published in the docs: ratio, write amplification, restore latency per tier.

Related doctrine: no-guarantees (storage is never assumed infinite), 10.a (censorship resistance — archival nodes as survival), the living roadmap (this lands on it).

Made-With: Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Partition the Postgres `event` ledger declaratively, age records through three operator-configured lossless tiers (raw hot window → aggressively compressed mid-tier → since-inception content-addressed archive), add an opt-in full-archival-node role, and publish ratio/write-amplification/restore benchmarks with bit-for-bit reconstruction tests.

### Evidence in the tree
- migrations/0002_event.sql:3 — `CREATE TABLE event (` is a plain heap table; there is no `PARTITION BY` clause anywhere in the file (or in any of the 11 migrations)
- migrations/0002_event.sql:24 — the only storage tuning is a single `event_payload_gin` index; no compression, no chunk table, no content-addressed segments
- migrations/0002_event.sql:27 — `CREATE RULE event_no_update` / `event_no_delete` keep the ledger append-only, but nothing moves or compacts rows
- docs/plans/data-model.md:809 — section heading is literally `## 6. Retention (planned)`
- docs/plans/data-model.md:811 — "Nothing is pruned, partitioned or garbage-collected today. Every table grows without bound, `event` is a single heap table (0002), and there is no `vibey gc` command. `vibey ledger` exposes only `show`. The intended policy, none of it implemented:"
- docs/architecture/decisions/0003-event-sourced-ledger.md:56 — "Partitioning `event` by `(project_id, cycle)` and a `vibey ledger archive` command are planned for when a project's ledger passes ~500k rows; neither exists yet (`vibey ledger` has only `show`)."
- …and 5 more

### What is actually left
- Write an ADR for the three-tier scheme (ADR-0003 only names partitioning as a future idea; CLAUDE.md requires an ADR plus, for the governing rule, a ratified sub-doctrine)
- Add a `[ledger]` config table to src/vibey/domain/config.py + infrastructure/config_loader.py exposing both tier-boundary Ns and the archival-node opt-in, and document it in docs/reference/configuration.md
- Write the migration that converts `event` to a declaratively partitioned table — this must preserve `event_seq`, the `append_event()` gapless-seq function, the `event_seq_uniq` constraint, the two no-update/no-delete rules and the `project(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` FK, all of which interact badly with partitioning
- Build automated partition rotation (creation, tier transition, archive fold-in) as a worker task or CLI command with zero operator ceremony
- Implement mid-tier compression with chunking + content-addressed hashing, and a `ledger_chunk` (or equivalent) table so identical chunks dedupe and archive verification is a hash walk
- Implement the archival tier as external content-addressed segment files, plus the fold-in producer
- Add `vibey ledger archive`, `restore` and `verify` subcommands (and their docs/reference/cli.md rows)
- Make `PostgresLedgerRepository.range()` / `all_for_project()` tier-aware so a query spanning raw + mid-tier + archive returns one coherent ordered answer
- …and 3 more

### Blockers
- No ADR or ratified sub-doctrine exists yet for the tier scheme, and CLAUDE.md makes both mandatory before this binds future decisions
- `append_event()` claims a gapless per-project seq inside the insert transaction (migrations/0002_event.sql:41) and rules R6 of the no-loss gate depend on it — partitioning the table is a real design decision, not a mechanical migration
- infrastructure/ and cli/ carry a 100% branch-coverage floor (ADR-0023), so every branch of the tier-transition and restore paths must be covered before CI goes green

**Notes:** Nothing in code implements any part of this. The only prior art is documentary and explicitly labelled unimplemented: ADR-0003 calls partitioning + `vibey ledger archive` "planned … neither exists yet", and data-model.md heads its section "Retention (planned)". This issue is the root dependency for #136's stated storage plan and for #137's shard/tier honesty requirement.

**Status: PARTIAL · planning size: XL**

The current revision contains ledger-tier foundations, migration work, and shard/search/hash-chain pieces. It does not yet demonstrate the complete raw-hot/mid-compressed/full-archive policy, optional archival node, rotation/sharding/chunk-hash behavior, benchmarks, and lossless round-trip acceptance.
